title: SIU clears York Region officers in fatal shooting
subtitle: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit says three York Region police officers were justified in the shooting death of a Thornhill man in August.
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit has cleared three York Region police officers in the fatal August shooting of a Thornhill man who stabbed his wife to death.
SIU director Ian Scott concluded that there are no reasonable grounds to charge the three officers in the Aug. 1 shooting of Kaveh Sabouri Tabatabaei, 49, of Cottonwood Crt.

According to the unit, three subject officers and five other police officers responded to an urgent 911 call regarding blood in a residence near Leslie and John Sts. After arriving, the officers forced their way into the home and found Tabatabaei's estranged spouse Nasrin Toreihi, 47, unconscious and lying on the kitchen floor, with multiple stab wounds.

Tabatabaei was found lying beside her, and he was holding the woman's hand. In his other hand he was holding a large kitchen knife, which he alternately used to stab himself, and swing at the officers.

The officers drew their guns and ordered Tabatabaei to drop his weapon. At the same time the officers were trying to reach the injured woman and protect her from him. The officers used a kitchen chair, a baton and even pepper-spray in a bid to subdue the man, all unsuccessfully.
None of the officers had been assigned a TASER.
Two officers shot Tabatabaei, who died at the scene.

Scott concluded the actions by the three subject officers were justified under a section of the Criminal Code that allows lethal force to prevent a serious offence that would likely cause immediate and serious injury to anyone else.

"The subject officers could reasonably believe that Mr. Tabatabaei was going to cause even more harm to (his estranged wife) by stabbing her again. Even if he did not attempt to stab her again, he was preventing the officers from rendering immediate aid to an individual who was in clear medical distress,'' Scott said in a statement.
